messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: dns-mesh-health | multiple probes failing in us-west-2 (AZ-b) — elevated 502/504s observed, initial signal threshold crossed. Trigger: 8 probes failed in 5m. @oncall-rotation paged.

alex.k: acked — I’m on it, pulling probe logs and flow logs. @maya can you grab routing table + LB metrics for us-west-2?

maya: on it. pulling ELB target health + NLB flow logs. quick note: our probe fleet uses both K8s sidecar probes and infra-level DNS probes. seeing gap on infra probes first.

julian: I’m checking the DNS mesh controller. At a glance controller reports healthy, but agent metrics show missing telemetry from workers in AZ-b since ~03:12 UTC. Could be a telemetry pipeline issue not actual DNS failures.

carol: support reported a customer incident (AcmeCorp) with sporadic 502s in the same window. Severity unclear until we validate whether it’s routing or probe false positives.

alex.k: workflow: 1) confirm whether probe failures correspond to actual customer errors (check access logs + 5xx counts), 2) verify VPC flow logs + ENI state in AZ-b, 3) if probe false-positive, mute alerts and re-enable after fix.

maya: ELB metrics: backend_5xx_count spiked ~03:10-03:18 in us-west-2, primarily from lb-usw2-prod-2. Target groups show ~20% unhealthy on one ASG in AZ-b. ENI list shows no detach events.

julian: DNS mesh agent logs: last heartbeat from worker-usw2-b-7 at 03:09, then nothing. k8s node shows as NotReady in cluster dashboard — kernel-level netstack reports intermittent NIC flaps.

carol: I pulled API gateway logs for AcmeCorp — 5xx traces correlate with backend timeouts, not DNS resolution failures. users are seeing latency then upstream timeout (502).

alex.k: hypothesis: localized NIC instabilities in AZ-b causing connection resets and LB target flapping; probe agents stop sending telemetry leading to alerts that look like DNS failures. Need to validate host-level NIC metrics.

oncall-rotation: reassigning to maya for mitigation and to julian for root cause. handoff scheduled, ETA 15m.

maya: mitigation steps in flight: 1) cordon & drain afflicted nodes in AZ-b (one ASG at a time), 2) shift traffic away from lb-usw2-prod-2 via weight adjustment, 3) temporarily increase probe thresholds for dns-mesh-health. Executing step 1 now.

julian: I’ll keep analyzing NIC logs and open a vendor ticket if hardware flaps persist. also enabling packet capture on one affected ENI.

incident-bot: runbook reminder: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/net-probe-failure — follow section: "AZ NIC instability".

maya: drain started on node worker-usw2-b-7 — pods draining; expecting reduced 5xx within next 60-120s as traffic shifts.

carol: notifying support: "We’re investigating a localized networking instability in us-west-2 AZ-b causing intermittent 502s. We’re shifting traffic and will update in 30m. Customers impacted: AcmeCorp and a small subset of API traffic"

alex.k: note for telemetry gap: logs show our probe aggregator stopped receiving pings from az-b agents at 03:10 but infra metrics (Cloud provider health events) show no region-level outage. This looks like host-level NIC flaps.

sre-automation-bot: telemetry anomaly detected: flow logs for subnet sn-usw2-apps-3 have no entries between 03:10 and 03:22; expected volume > 1200 entries/min.

julian: packet capture shows frequent TCP RSTs originating from worker NIC; vendor NIC firmware counters show increased rx_errors. Opening hardware ticket with cloud provider (case #CP-88122).

maya: mitigation progress: shifted 60% of LB weight to us-west-2 AZ-c and AZ-a. backend_5xx_count dropping — down to baseline in last 2 mins.

carol: support acked that AcmeCorp errors decreased after traffic shift; they asked for an incident summary and ETA for full remediation.

alex.k: immediate customer impact: intermittent 502s for ~12-18 minutes, affecting ~18% of requests in us-west-2, specific customers notified via support. Incident classification: partial regional degradation (AZ-localized).

oncall-rotation: handoff to julian for long-term RCA and follow-up. maya retains action to reintroduce drained nodes once cloud vendor confirms hardware stable.

julian: next steps: 1) vendor to replace/repair NICs or migrate instances, 2) validate probe agent reconnection and telemetry backfill, 3) revert probe threshold temp change, 4) postmortem in incidents channel with timeline + mitigation + long-term fixes (e.g., cross-AZ redundancy for probe fleet).

maya: adding config note: consider increasing cross-AZ replication of probe agents and adding a secondary telemetry path (push vs pull) to avoid single-path telemetry loss.

carol: I’ll prepare customer-facing summary and liaise with account team.

alex.k: summary for postmortem start: cause suspected host NIC instability in us-west-2 AZ-b leading to probe telemetry loss and target flapping; mitigation was traffic reweight + node drains; customer impact limited and reduced after mitigation. Assigning owners: julian (RCA), maya (mitigation + node recovery), carol (customer comms).

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated — ETA to full recovery pending vendor confirmation. Tags: network, telemetry-gap, us-west-2, AZ-b.

julian: logging ticket numbers + notes, will draft postmortem. closing thread here, will re-open if vendor confirms broader issue. :thumbsup:
